description: Transport-neutral ARPG core composition over its embedded Rapier physics. The product contract protects complete command/tick/snapshot orchestration, physics included, without physics microbenchmarks or game-server transport benchmarks.

scenarios.description: Drive four players through deterministic movement, periodic attacks, physics stepping and regular snapshots for one simulated minute.
correctnessEvidence: identical final ArpgSnapshot across repeated runs

metrics.name: snapshot_materializations
metrics.notes: Counted by the operation-work feature; the journey requests one snapshot every 60 ticks. The blocking per-tick bound is the ordinary-tick and requested-snapshot operations.

metrics.name: monster_target_evaluations
metrics.notes: Counted by the operation-work feature. The blocking candidate/search bound is the monster-targeting operation.

scenarios.description: Future game-server integration evidence should measure serialization/snapshot/reconnect composition separately from ARPG core stepping.
correctnessEvidence: same authoritative ArpgSnapshot crosses local/browser/dedicated hosting seams

metrics.name: snapshot_bytes
metrics.notes: Add when the game-server adapter exposes a stable benchmark fixture; do not move transport logic into arpg-core to obtain this metric.

operations.description: Advance 60 authoritative ticks without a snapshot request while every player re-sends movement every 15 ticks. Four monsters fight the players in the active encounter; the rest wait in dormant rooms.

players.description: connected players, all in the active encounter room

monsters.description: monsters in the world: four in the active encounter, the rest in the four dormant rooms, at most eight (one encounter) per room

metrics.name: physics_steps_per_tick
metrics.notes: Largest number of physics passes in one tick of the window; their cost is part of the complete tick.

metrics.name: ticks_without_one_physics_step
metrics.notes: Ticks of the window that did not step physics exactly once.

metrics.name: snapshot_materializations
metrics.notes: Authoritative snapshots built during the window; encoding needs one, so zero also rules out serialization.

operations.description: Materialize one requested authoritative snapshot of a world with four players and four engaged monsters, the rest dormant. Output work is linear in exported entities.

monsters.description: monsters in the world, each exported in the snapshot: four engaged, the rest at most eight per dormant room

metrics.name: snapshot_entities_materialized
metrics.notes: Rooms, doors, players, monsters, loot, colliders, arrows, chests and events written into the snapshot.

operations.description: Advance 60 ticks of engagement decisions with idle players inside aggro range of the engaged monsters. Only free monsters of an active encounter decide, and each scores the living players (at most four); dormant monsters elsewhere are unrelated population.

players.description: living players, all candidates of every deciding monster

engagedMonsters.description: monsters in the players' active encounter room, at most eight (one encounter)

unrelatedMonsters.description: monsters in the four dormant rooms without players, at most eight (one encounter) per room

metrics.name: monster_decisions_per_tick
metrics.notes: Largest number of engagement-policy decisions in one tick of the window.

metrics.name: monster_target_evaluations_per_tick
metrics.notes: Largest number of target candidates scored in one tick. The intended bound is deciding monsters times living players; a scan of the whole world grows with unrelatedMonsters.

operations.description: Apply one movement command for one player to a world with four players and four engaged monsters while the dormant population grows. Domain work a command causes, such as a target-lock search, is outside this bookkeeping bound.

unrelatedMonsters.description: monsters in the four dormant rooms without players, at most eight (one encounter) per room

metrics.name: command_bookkeeping_steps
metrics.notes: Player validation, lane sequence check and lane watermark record.
